venue.name: Emily Carr House
venue.description: Emily Carr House is a provincial and national historic site in Victoria, the birthplace and childhood home of the Canadian artist and writer Emily Carr. The restored house and its gardens now operate as a cultural centre for education and community creativity, offering guided tours, school programs, events and workshops. The house displays reproductions rather than original Carr paintings, because it does not have the environmental controls originals require.
venue.address: 207 Government St, Victoria, British Columbia V8V 2K8

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The first floor of the house is wheelchair accessible; the accessible entrance is at the rear of the house down a gravel path. The second floor is only accessible by stairs.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Parking on the property is limited to 3 vehicles by the front fence, and the roundabout must stay clear for emergency vehicles, but visitors may be dropped off at the door. Free three-hour parking at Beacon Hill Park along Douglas Street.

venue.nearby_park: Beacon Hill Park, which the site names for free three-hour parking along Douglas Street. The house is a 10-minute walk from the Inner Harbour.
restrictions: As a historical site Carr House cannot allow pets into the house, with the exception of certified guide/service dogs. Pets are, however, welcome in the gardens.
The house holds reproductions, not original Emily Carr paintings.
venue.hours_notes: Summer hours June 3 to August 30 2026: Wednesday-Sunday 10 am to 5 pm. Fall hours September 3 to Dec 13 2026: Thursday-Saturday 10 am to 4 pm. Hours can change during private events; the site asks visitors to call 250-383-5843 to confirm.
venue.seasonal_notes: The site publishes only summer and fall 2026 windows (June 3 to August 30, then September 3 to December 13). Nothing is published about opening between mid-December and early June.

programs.name: School group programs
programs.description: Educational programs for school groups, described on the site as ranging from guided tours to scavenger hunts. Booking is by an enquiry form on the School Groups page, whose message field asks for number of students, age and date.
programs.what_children_do: Go through the house where Emily Carr was born and spent her childhood, either on a guided tour or working through a scavenger hunt in its rooms. The site does not describe the programs in any more detail than that.
programs.our_note: The site confirms school programs exist but publishes no price, age range, group size or notice period, so the enquiry form is the only way to find any of it out. Send it well before you need an answer, and ask for all four in one message.
programs.practical_summary: The first floor is wheelchair accessible by a rear gravel path and the second floor is stairs only, so plan for a group that may not all see the whole house. Washrooms, lunch space and rain backup are not stated anywhere on the site.
programs.evidence: Carr House offers a range of educational programs for school groups, from guided tours to scavenger hunts.

programs.name: Carr House guided tour
programs.description: A 40-minute staff-led tour of the house, booked in advance through the venue's Eventbrite page. The Plan Your Visit page gives the schedule as Fridays and Saturdays at 10 a.m., 12 p.m. and 2 p.m., and notes that special events may disrupt it.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the rooms of the house with a trained staff member and hear stories about Emily Carr's childhood and family life.
programs.our_note: Forty minutes standing and listening is the whole visit here, and the tour runs only on Fridays and Saturdays, so it suits older groups more than a preschool room. Admission is by donation, which means you should agree an amount internally before you arrive.
programs.practical_summary: Three fixed start times on Fridays and Saturdays, 40 minutes each, booked through Eventbrite rather than the venue directly. No group rate, capacity or minimum notice is published.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission is by donation; the site publishes no set price for the guided tour.
programs.evidence: Please sign up in advance on Eventbrite for a 40-minute tour

programs.name: Self-guided visit
programs.description: Visitors may drop in during open hours and go through the house at their own pace, with no booking required. Tour information is available on entry.
programs.what_children_do: Move through the rooms of the house at their own pace, reading the information handed out at the door.
programs.our_note: This is the flexible option: no booking, no fixed start time, and you set the pace, which matters with young children who may not last a full guided tour. Check the hours before you go, because they are seasonal and change during private events.
programs.practical_summary: Drop-in during open hours, admission by donation, no booking needed. Hours are seasonal and the site asks you to phone ahead to confirm.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission is by donation; no amount is published.
programs.evidence: Visitors may drop in to tour the house at their own pace.
